diagnostics.message: When google_organization_iam_binding.authoritative grants a custom role created by google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles, the role must exist before the binding is applied. The role currently comes from a variable map key, so Terraform can create the binding before the custom role or delete the custom role before removing its binding. Resolve locally managed role names through the custom-role resources, preserving externally supplied role names as a fallback.

fix.expression: lookup({ for role_id, role in google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles : "organizations/${local.organization_id_numeric}/roles/${role_id}" => role.name }, each.key, each.key)

diagnostics.message: When google_organization_iam_member.additive grants a custom role created by google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles, that role must exist before the membership is applied. Reading each.value.role from the input-derived map does not establish this ordering. Reference the managed role's name when it matches the requested role, retaining the input for external roles.

fix.expression: lookup({ for role_id, role in google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles : "organizations/${local.organization_id_numeric}/roles/${role_id}" => role.name }, each.value.role, each.value.role)

diagnostics.message: When google_organization_iam_policy.authoritative includes roles created by google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles, applying the policy must wait for those custom roles to exist. Its dependency on data.google_iam_policy.authoritative only waits for policy JSON generation from input values; it does not order creation of the custom roles. Add an explicit dependency on the custom-role resources to prevent a role-not-found race and preserve reverse destroy ordering.
